survey: A traditional straw broom floats diagonally as a standalone icon on a wavy blue background, with no surface to rest on. The wooden handle runs from upper right to lower left. It is straight, evenly thick and ends in a rounded knob cap at the top. At the bottom the handle goes into the bristle head, held by a binding: a yellow cord wrap above two red rope wraps, coiled tightly around the neck where the straw bunches onto the handle. The bristle head is a bundle of straw clumps that flares out from the binding and ends in a softly rounded, slightly tucked tip line. It lines up with the handle's axis and faces the camera at a three-quarter angle. Every part connects to the next: knob to handle, handle into binding, binding around the bristle neck. Nothing passes through anything else, and there are no extra or missing parts. The wraps show no free cord ends, which is an acceptable simplification. Floating is fine because this is an isolated item icon, not a scene. Stylized clumped bristles with rounded tips are a common card simplification and do not stop it from working as a broom.
